rca_of_the_issue: SeoHead RCA: setTag() builds selector `meta[name='description'][data-seo-head]`. On first mount, this query returns null (no such tag exists), so SeoHead creates a NEW <meta> with data-seo-head=true. The original <meta name='description'> from index.html still sits earlier in <head>. Standard DOM query `document.querySelector('meta[name=description]')` returns the FIRST match — the static one. Same for og:title, og:image, canonical. Google/Twitter/Facebook crawlers reading <head> top-to-bottom also see the static one first. Mitigation: SeoHead must either (1) hijack the existing static tag (set content, mark with data-seo-head, remember original for cleanup), or (2) remove the static defaults from index.html and let SeoHead own everything. Approach (1) is safer because it preserves SEO baseline if SeoHead fails to mount.
